EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong band at 1344 cm⁻¹ that coincides with the characteristic symmetric νs(NO₂) stretch (rule GFQ-022). A companion asymmetric νas(NO₂) band is expected near 1500–1550 cm⁻¹; the observed 1458 cm⁻¹ band is consistent with a red-shifted νas(NO₂) often seen in aliphatic nitro compounds. Among the candidates, only molecule 4 (CCC(CO)(CO)[N+](=O)[O-]) contains an aliphatic –NO₂ group.  

The intense C–H stretches at 2880–2964 cm⁻¹ match the many sp³ C–H bonds in this tert-butyl framework. Additional medium peaks at 1083, 965, 948 and 923 cm⁻¹ are compatible with C–O and C–C skeletal/rocking modes of primary alcohol groups present in candidate 4. No other listed molecule bears an –NO₂ group, making candidate 4 the best fit to the diagnostic 1344 cm⁻¹ feature and overall aliphatic pattern.
